outcome: Terms updated 24 July 2026 establish cohort-specific commitment periods; the legacy blanket rule for earlier customers is corrected.
Current 30GB JPY2,970/month remains valid through 2026-11-30; official ahamo materials schedule a tiered JPY3,135/40GB entry plan from 2026-12-01.

AIS local prepaid supports eSIM/passport identity handling and provider prepaid offers can add service-validity days. 2026 community users report low monthly keep costs and fast SMS reception, but stronger multi-year low-cost extension claims remain unverified against current provider rules.
Current official support separates a 180-day chargeable-use rule from a 180-day top-up/plan credit rule; the old £5/180-day model is not safe to publish as a settled minimum.

CIN 1 remains documented at AZN3.99/30 days with one-way blocking after expiry if neither the fee nor a top-up is made, plus an AZN0.99/6-day extension option, but CIN 1 now appears in Bakcell’s tariff archive rather than the current GO tariff surface.

Users reported SIM in Safe disappearing from the app and remote re-activation failing after technical changes; support reportedly confirmed the service could still be attached even when not visible. Treat remote enablement/status visibility as a live operational risk.

Current policy establishes a 90-day no-transaction restriction followed by 275 days of office-restorable retention before termination. China roaming and international top-up are current for eligible prepaid lines, while the foreigner-specific Hello product is local-only and cannot be assumed equivalent to the roaming-capable ordinary prepaid route.

Current BH Telecom webshop material establishes the Ultra top-up validity ladder and a 150-day post-credit number-retention/recovery period; visitor eSIM products and foreign-issued-card top-ups are current.

BTC prepaid remains current and legacy prepaid plans were replaced in 2025, but current number lifecycle, minimum keep-alive action, foreigner acquisition and China-specific prepaid roaming remain unresolved.
The product and same-number extension path are current: 3GB annual entry is now ¥7,860 and the dedicated extension product is ¥5,400, with SMS reception and extension support explicitly listed.

Current Cellcard official surfaces conflict on the post-expiry top-up recovery window: the English business/self-service terms say expired balance can be restored by top-up within 30 calendar days, while the current Khmer main-site terms state 180 days. Do not infer number-retention/recycling timing from either balance-recovery window until reconciled.

Legacy GEL2/year was a rough estimate. Current official unit pricing and 90-day lifecycle imply a lower theoretical paid-action floor, but passive incoming SMS should not be relied on as the reset action.

The 180-day lifecycle is current and confirmed, but the legacy NT$100/NT$200-per-year floor was not re-established as the current minimum qualifying recharge. Preserve the lifecycle and leave the minimum cost unresolved.
Claro terms establish 180-day recharge validity plus a 60-day active grace period; current foreigner acquisition and prepaid roaming paths are also documented.
The legacy 90-day recharge and recycle timing could not be independently reverified against current 2026 Claro pages in this round. Preserve it only as a HOLD signal, not a current-guaranteed rule.

Current Claro Chile prepaid evidence establishes subscriber identification and a 180-day total recharge/recovery window, but current foreign-passport new-line activation, prepaid overseas SMS behavior and foreign-card recharge execution remain unresolved.

Current Claro Colombia prepaid evidence establishes a COP1,000 recharge floor, 60-day recharge validity, line-deactivation risk after 60 days without movements and free incoming roaming SMS in supported prepaid destinations; foreign-user initial registration and mainland-China coverage remain unresolved.

Current CMLink UK promotion explicitly advertises GBP15/year for 365 days of number holding. 2026 community reports preserve material operational constraints: customer-service or plan-history eligibility may be required, and retention/one-time-plan expiry can be followed by a roughly 30-day no-plan closure window.

Current official FROG terms retain the number for up to 13 months from activation/last balance renewal, while the current electronic minimum top-up for FROG is EUR13; the legacy EUR10 keep-alive estimate is withdrawn.

Cricket 12-month Unlimited remains USD300 prepaid; unpaid service is suspended with a 60-day number-recovery boundary. Cricket Passport now includes China, while Wi-Fi Calling requires prior Cricket-network attachment and China-first acquisition/payment remain unresolved.

The current csl product page lists 180-day base validity and a promotional recharge table where HKD20-49.9 or more extends validity 365 days through 31 Dec 2026, but the same page's terms also state HKD50+ extends validity 180 days. The route is therefore normalized as HOLD rather than assigning one universal keep interval or annual cost.

CTExcel UK and its Back to China SIM Retention Plan are current. Community evidence repeatedly reports a 90-day activity rule for some no-plan accounts but also plan-dependent retention and conflicting post-plan behavior. The provider-visible pages do not cleanly expose current retention eligibility, price and post-expiry mechanics, so no universal lifecycle or annual keep cost is asserted.

Current provider eSIM center lists Easy Pass as a prepaid eSIM product and supports designated physical-SIM-to-eSIM conversion for eligible existing customers; a September 2026 independent user report reproduces successful conversion.

Current provider FAQ states Greater Bay Area prepaid is valid 180 days from activation; a recharge during validity extends/reset validity to 180 days from the recharge date; zero balance or expiry suspends service; more than 90 days continuously suspended causes automatic cancellation.

Current Easy PASS brochure states incoming SMS is free in Macau, mainland China and Hong Kong. This proves ordinary incoming-SMS capability only; service-specific bank/app OTP reliability remains unverified in this review.

Current Cyta material resolves the legacy gap: EUR 5, 10, 20, 35 or 50 credit top-ups each grant 365 days; after the 365-day deadline outgoing service stops, followed by 7 days incoming-only and 15 additional days before number cancellation.
Legacy LKR500/365d was not found in the current official ladder. Current documented options are LKR400/180d and LKR1000/365d; exact additive stacking behavior remains a caveat.
Current CelcomDigi documentation directly confirms Digi RM100=120-day reload validity and an explicit RM198/365-day validity extension.

Current Digicel terms establish deactivation after four months with no usage and new-number assignment after reactivation; current visitor acquisition, international top-up and China roaming exist, but the exact clock-resetting keep-alive action is unresolved.

DITO prepaid/eSIM is current and community users in 2026 report very low annual keep-alive costs, but foreign-tourist registration and the 30-day Traveler SIM lifecycle are binding provider constraints; the claimed PHP5/PHP10 annual regular-load extension was not confirmed by a current provider lifecycle table in this review.

Current provider instructions resolve the legacy validity gap: three months from first activation, twelve months after every recharge, then a one-month expired window in which incoming calls/messages and recharging remain possible.

Provider currently states that the +372 phone-number eSIM supports calls/SMS, has no monthly bill, balance does not expire, and stays active with at least one use per year. September 2026 community users reproduced China-side signal and several verification SMS outcomes but also reported prefix-dependent failures.

The old AED10-per-quarter framing is not needed for the current normalized rule. Current e& pages state lifetime validity with continued use and a 12-month retention/revival window after non-use; exact minimum annual cash cost is therefore left unresolved.

Current Fortress FAQ establishes 365-day validity after activation and another 365 days after a top-up of at least HKD10. Current FAQ also documents real-name registration, physical-SIM-only service, voice/SMS behavior and number-recycling caveats; 2026 community users continue to report HK retail availability and HKD10 annual maintenance.

The €2/month plan remains current, but eligibility is expressly limited to people residing in metropolitan France or able to justify a stable link with metropolitan France; it is not a general non-resident acquisition route.
newly obtained number appeared associated with a prior Telegram account
multiple overseas users reported closures/suspensions and loss of service
some previously closed accounts/numbers were restored; not universal
multiple eventual refund successes observed after delays or earlier denials; outcome remains mixed

GO PAYG resets its inactivity clock with a top-up or chargeable event; 90 days without one enters a 275-day grace period, after which the SIM disconnects unless reactivated. Visitor eSIM can be obtained through the GO app before arrival and PAYG roaming is enabled on activation.
The legacy $20/180-day mechanism traces to old Petro-Canada-era evidence and is not supported by a current Good2Go provider rule in this audit; post-network-transition structure remains unresolved.

Flexible remains USD20/month + USD10/GB, China is in the international destination list with free texts, but Fi requires a valid U.S. payments address and at least one day of U.S. activation/use before international service; extended overseas data remains restricted.

Legacy BDT995/5-year claim is stale. Current first-party surfaces show approximately BDT1497-1498 for five-year account validity, with a BDT1 discrepancy between official pages. Keep BDT300/365-day recharge as the clean current floor until the five-year price conflict is reconciled.

Current csl HK Mobi page gives 365-day card validity and a promotional HKD20-or-more recharge ladder extending card validity by 365 days through 31 Dec 2026. csl also requires real-name registration; long-running community evidence corroborates the HKD20 annual renewal mechanic and current eSIM/MNP use.

Current Israeli recharge retailers consistently advertise a HOTALK 66 ILS pay-per-use balance load with 180-day validity, but current first-party evidence tying that balance validity to the phone-number deactivation/recycling lifecycle was not located. The legacy no-KYC claim is also withdrawn as unverified.

Current PAYG legal terms permit disconnection after four months without credit, a bundle or a chargeable event and expire unused credit after 365 days without an additional top-up. Current iD marketing/community wording also says 180 days, so the conflict is preserved rather than silently choosing the looser interval.
Current IF Mobile pricing remains available, but the prior remote image-plus-selfie identity flow ended 2026-03-31; current nonresident remote signup and mainland-China SMS utility remain unresolved.
Current provider evidence confirms JPY850/month 2GB voice pricing, Japan-address/identity/payment gating, and overseas voice/SMS availability for voice SIM/eSIM.

Current Jazz material resolves foreigner purchase requirements and prepaid roaming/incoming-SMS pricing, but SIM Lagao is only a 60-day reactivation promotion and does not establish final number-lifecycle or minimum keep-alive economics.

kölbi terms tie 90 days without a chargeable main-balance event or recharge to definitive liquidation and number disposal; current tourist/passport acquisition and China roaming make the route usable as backstage evidence without inventing a cheapest annual cost.

KT now provides an exact recharge-validity ladder up to KRW50,000/365 days, but passport-only usage is short-term/90-day constrained without further identity verification and Welcome Prepaid excludes roaming.
The 274-day active plus 91-day suspension rule and UAH30 restoration threshold are supported by current operator material and 2026 enforcement reporting.
Current LABAS rules directly confirm the €3/90-day account rule and 120-day hard number-loss boundary.

Lebara France currently runs on SFR. Top-ups from EUR5 are described as valid for 90 days, but contract summaries separately permit termination after 90 consecutive days without service use; the legacy EUR15/90-day top-up-only retention claim is withdrawn.
inbound verification SMS worked while outgoing SMS/voice/Wi-Fi Calling were initially incomplete or conflicting

Current LG U+ first-party evidence resolves a visitor SIM with a 010 number, while a separate LG U+ network MVNO (U+ UMobile) carries the long-term prepaid product. The legacy route identity is therefore not safely attributable to one current product, and the MVNO prepaid plans list roaming as unavailable.

Current LINEMO pricing, resident-foreigner identity requirements, contract fee and overseas SMS mechanics are documented; new-number lines cannot enroll in World Support until the fifth billing month.
LMT confirms a 60-day advance-validity plus 60-day receive-only structure and a €1 online refill minimum, but the old €3 every 60 days / €18-year model does not follow from the current pages.

Current provider catalog establishes a 1095-day Hong Kong-number plan at HKD138 and a durable top-up ladder where HKD50 extends number expiry 180 days, HKD100 extends 365 days, and HKD200 extends 540 days. The prior lifecycle blocker is cleared; the cheapest simple verified ongoing annual keep action is HKD100 for 365 days.

Recent independent evidence supports overseas incoming SMS and ordinary mainland-China SMS, but bank and third-party OTP reliability remains insufficiently sampled. Preserve HOLD and do not publish an OTP guarantee or success percentage.

The 120-day / £15 annual keep-number mechanism has fresh independent corroboration, and the legacy O2 host-network field is stale: current UK service runs on EE. The UK first-party FAQ text was not retrievable in this audit.
Independent 2026 reports confirm the AT&T migration and include service/account/SIM-swap failures during transition. These are incident evidence, not a route-wide failure rate.

Current official terms retain the 60-day non-use expiry. A current 12-month 8 GB plan is USD 108, so the old USD 120/year claim is not a valid minimum-retention fact; exact PAYG keep-alive cost remains unresolved.
Provider charges 1 GEL at service activation on a new number and the next 1 GEL on day 181. Treat ~2.03 GEL/year as the annualized 180-day run-rate, not an exact first-year cash-total guarantee.

Current JAWAL terms establish a 12-month card validity renewed by each recharge, SIM/eSIM support and identity-backed activation. Recent visitor-eSIM reports preserve real tourist acquisition plus fulfillment friction; foreign-passport long-term eligibility is not inferred from generic identity-document language.

Current Mint terms establish suspension at plan expiry and cancellation/reassignment risk after 60 days without successful renewal while suspended. The 12-month 6GB plan remains USD180/year. Official Wi-Fi Calling is usable abroad, while reliable China-first activation/payment and standalone China cellular SMS/OTP remain unresolved.

Tourist prepaid acquisition explicitly accepts a foreign passport, but the Number Retention page says outlet enrollment or a letter enclosing NIC. Foreign-passport holder retention enrollment, especially remotely, remains unresolved.

Current prepaid contract ties recharge to active service and permits cancellation after seven months without recharge; current foreign-national acquisition is in-person/biometric, while prepaid-specific overseas SMS and China behavior remain unresolved.

MTN Number For Life provides 12- or 24-month prepaid number reservation and current prepaid roaming supports SMS, but MTN-specific foreign-user registration guidance conflicts with the regulator’s foreign-prepaid path.

Current MTN prices are NGN3,500/1 year, NGN5,000/2 years and NGN7,500/3 years. Current prepaid terms also establish a visitor registration path without NIN for stays under 24 months, subject to valid visa and passport/travel documentation.

MTS Belarus withdraws a number after 60 days without top-up following forced blocking, or after 180 days with a positive balance but no operations; however the current guest tariff explicitly disables roaming and SMS roaming for foreign citizens/stateless persons.

MTS support updated in 2026 confirms the Сохраняю номер service exists for eligible no-monthly-fee tariffs and that most lines face termination after roughly six months without qualifying top-up or spend. The product-price page remains geo-fragile, so tariff eligibility should stay constrained.
Ncell now documents both the visitor acquisition path and the long-duration prepaid recharge-validity ladder; China roaming is current, while application-specific OTP behavior remains unverified.

A 300–499 CZK top-up gives only six months of credit validity, but O2 separately states the prepaid SIM/card itself remains valid for 12 months from the last top-up. Do not confuse credit expiry with number/SIM expiry.

Current Omantel agreement establishes 90-day prepaid validity plus a 90-day number-holding period; current Hayyak supports passport eSIM acquisition, card/app recharge and free incoming SMS while roaming.

Current provider pages establish a 90-day active window, EUR2 online top-up floor and an extended tourist-eSIM recharge grace period, while roaming terms explicitly exclude Tourist Package users from roaming outside Montenegro.

Current One NZ terms make Prepay credit expire 360 days after top-up and the service inactive with number loss if no new credit is added. Minimum logged-in website/app top-up is NZD10. Physical Prepay activation requires One NZ mobile coverage; China is a current Prepay roaming destination, while service-specific OTP reliability is not guaranteed.

Current Hala evidence establishes a QAR10 minimum recharge, 30-day active credit validity followed by 179 days of grace before line deactivation, passport/QID verification and current prepaid roaming coverage including China; OTP reliability remains unverified.

Legacy A$59/186-day and A$180/365-day retention economics are stale. Current official long-expiry options are A$180/186 days and A$350/365 days, while Optus states the 365-day A$350 price rises to A$395 on 2026-09-30.

Current Orange rules confirm the active/grace ladder and show the legacy €42/year estimate was not defensible: a €5 recharge grants 30 active days plus 300 grace days, while grace can receive calls/SMS.

The previously unresolved fee is now explicit: XOF 3,000/6 months, XOF 5,000/12 months and XOF 10,000/24 months. Subscription is available via airtime USSD or Orange Money, and the extension starts on the subscription date.

Current Proximus pages say Pay&Go is valid 12 months after first call and >EUR5 top-up extends 12 months, but the current FAQ separately says a card not used for more than 6 months is automatically deactivated. The reviewed page does not define exactly which activity satisfies “used”; annual top-up alone must not be treated as sufficient.

Current Rakuten pricing and overseas service are documented, while foreign-customer onboarding remains a Japanese-residence-document path and Rakuten Link should be initialized in Japan before travel.
The annual product remains current, but the legacy $60/$30 economics are stale. Current Essentials is $80 first year and renews at $110/year; activation must occur in the United States.

Daima pricing remains directly documented on Safaricom pages: KSh200/6 months, KSh500/1 year and KSh1000/2 years. The product pages are older, so continued live availability remains a monitoring item.

Current Saily documentation establishes a persistent dedicated U.S. +1 number with calls/SMS, while explicitly identifying the underlying carrier technology as internet-based/VoIP. The route is therefore normalized as a non-cellular VoIP second line rather than a carrier-mobile SIM or a data-only eSIM.

An independent user reported that the purchased Saily phone-number/SMS feature never became operational despite repeated troubleshooting and two installation attempts; another commenter reported a similar failure. Preserve this as HOLD evidence rather than treating provider availability as proof of operational reliability.
Current SK Telecom material establishes the PPS recharge lifecycle, passport onboarding and stay-expiry recharge constraint; current roaming guidance classifies PPS as roaming-unavailable.

A February 2026 independent community thread starts from a fully activated Smart prepaid eSIM and includes a user reporting that Smart service worked for them in Australia. Preserve this as weak practical roaming evidence only; it is not a service-specific OTP success record.

Smart ordinary prepaid lifecycle remains 365 days for loaded value plus a 180-day reload grace after balance reaches zero, but foreign tourists face a separate 30-day SIM-registration validity cap unless an approved visa extension is supplied. The legacy route is therefore not treated as a generally available long-term foreign-user route.

A September 29-October 1, 2026 community thread reports multiple Smart eSIM activation/conversion failures, including no-service and lost OTP/call reception after physical-to-eSIM conversion. Treat this as a dated operational incident signal, not proof of a permanent platform-wide failure.

A September 2026 community report says a PHP99 Smart eSIM bought through the app produced a QR code that activated immediately. This is a single acquisition/activation report and does not override foreign-tourist registration limits.

Smart instructs prepaid users to activate roaming before departure by sending ROAM ON to 333. Smart still requires PHP100 balance for roaming activation, but its current reload guidance says the former PHP50 maintaining balance while abroad is no longer required and roaming can remain active without load.

Smart currently documents prepaid international roaming with text service: in supported voice-roaming countries prepaid users can make and receive calls and texts, and in countries without prepaid voice roaming they may still send and receive SMS. This confirms roaming-SMS capability but does not establish service-specific OTP reliability.

Current SMARTY material resolves the old monthly-payment-only assumption: a plan can remain inactive before automatic account closure at 220 days, while current China roaming explicitly lists free incoming SMS; active service must be renewed before relying on calls/text/data.

Current StarHub Prepaid is a monthly-plan product with a 120-day post-expiry grace period. Passport-only prepaid registration is limited to 30 days unless re-registered using an eligible Singapore-issued identity/work pass; the legacy cheap-USSD/top-up retention model is withdrawn.

Current STC personal prepaid terms document 180-day SIM validity from paid activity, while a still-live STC recharge page says 360 days; non-citizen final-departure/ID-expiry cancellation remains a structural blocker.

Historical Talkmobile PAYG ended on 31 August 2017; current Talkmobile sells contract/SIM-only plans only, so the PAYG route remains preserved as discontinued negative knowledge rather than remapped to a current subscription.
Current Telekom rules replace the legacy recurring 90-day assumption: the first top-up is due within 90 days of activation, then each top-up extends the SIM and nominal credit by 180 days.

Current Free2Go material establishes active acquisition, a EUR 5 recharge floor and the 90/180/270-day lifecycle; general prepaid terms allow SIM disconnection after day 270, while China OTP remains unverified.

Current Telenor Kontant uses a 12-month clock from the last recharge, followed by a two-month automatic reopening window. Current self-service access requires Telenor ID/BankID and web recharge cards are limited to Nordic-issued cards, so nonresident acquisition and maintenance remain constrained.

Current Telenor support confirms registered prepaid numbers and destination-specific prepaid roaming, while current purchase/recharge economics and foreign-user registration remain unresolved; legacy cheap annual pricing is withdrawn.
The legacy Telia DK prepaid label now conflicts with the current Norlys Mobil consumer surface; no current Telia-branded prepaid product/lifecycle was located, so the route remains HOLD.
Current Super guidance directly confirms the 180-day validity rule, EUR3 single-top-up threshold, 30-day receive-only recovery window, and eSIM starter availability.

Legacy Rp5,000/year keep-cost inference is unsupported by current rules. Rp5,000 top-up is not documented as a 365-day extension; official extension options include Rp115,000/360 days, while qualifying usage/top-up/package rules may yield cheaper paths whose durable annual minimum remains unresolved.

Legacy 4p-text / GBP0.08-year keep estimate belonged to retired PAYG pricing. Current Essentials standard SMS is 10p, so a two-actions-per-year theoretical floor is about GBP0.20 after the required initial top-up.

Tigo Tanzania is now Yas Tanzania with core services/contracts continued; current Yas terms allow suspension/re-allocation after 90 days non-use and current roaming lists China, while TCRA visitor registration is limited to visitors staying no more than four months.

Connect remains USD15/month for 5GB. Current prepaid support allows cancellation and number loss after more than 120 days in Not Paid status. Current prepaid roaming publishes USD0.10 incoming SMS outside Canada, includes China in the country table and provides no prepaid data roaming.

The legacy THB35/90d and THB70/180d validity-extension mechanism remains useful community intelligence, but current 2026 first-party terms were not reachable. Keep the row as HOLD and do not present the price as current-guaranteed.

Tune Talk currently offers RM35 for 365-day validity on listed prepaid plans, but Malaysia's 26 Feb 2026 mandatory prepaid-registration standard limits tourist-registered SIMs to a maximum three months before automatic termination. The one-year validity mechanism is preserved for eligible subscriptions without representing it as a durable tourist route.
Light remains USD 10 monthly or USD 96/year. Native roaming cannot work until the line has domestic U.S. usage; Warp/Dark Star Wi-Fi Calling setup also requires U.S. coverage.
Legacy GS2 pricing was community-only; the current VinaPhone GS2 product page directly supports VND120,000 for a 360-day validity extension.

Visible base remains USD25/month or USD275/year. Current terms suspend nonpayment-deactivated service for 60 days before cancellation/reassignment. Official Wi-Fi Calling works internationally when enabled before leaving the U.S.; current independent evidence corroborates long-duration use abroad, while overseas first activation remains contradictory.

Legacy 83-day inactivity and 100-day recycle summary is not the current first-party rule. Current Vodacom prepaid terms say suspension/disconnection may occur after service has not been used for more than 110 days. Exact final recycle timing remains unresolved.

Vodafone Egypt prepaid foreigner KYC and prepaid roaming are current, but Park Your Line is explicitly a postpaid service and Tourist Line is a separate visitor product; neither establishes generic prepaid long-term number retention.

Current Vodafone NL prepaid keeps credit and number active with at least one paid call, SMS, mobile-data session or top-up every six months; after six months of inactivity there is a three-month frozen-credit recovery window. Current community evidence shows overseas acquisition/payment variability and successful SMS/OTP reception, while China-specific cellular OTP reliability remains evidence-scoped.

The legacy route ID/brand refers to Vodafone TUTI. The current provider surface is One Hungary and the active product is Tuti Feltöltőkártya. Preserve the legacy ID for comparison continuity but use the current One/Tuti product identity.
Current Yettel material resolves SIM validity and online top-up, but the available digital-registration instructions document selfie plus ID-card capture rather than a verified foreign-passport path.
Yettel explicitly says top-up sent from another Yettel prepaid/postpaid number does not prolong card expiry. Use a standard top-up channel for lifecycle renewal.

Current eeZee supports a KD13 365-day validity extension, KD5 new prepaid voice line, expatriate passport/Civil-ID purchase, eSIM, remote recharge and prepaid voice/SMS roaming by default; China-specific OTP remains unverified.

Independent evidence now includes one user who continued receiving Hong Kong SMS for banking codes while in Australia, plus a separate 2026 report of weeks without receiving Hong Kong SMS until LuckySIM support restarted the connection. This is mixed route-level evidence: it strengthens the existence of overseas banking-code reception but does not establish a specific bank, broad OTP reliability, or stable delivery. Preserve HOLD.

Seven distinct dated community threads now support a Telegram registration-verification aggregate for ClubSIM. Outcomes remain mixed across prefix, client, proxy/IP and roaming conditions; this is evidence of variability, not a universal carrier success probability.

Five distinct dated public community/demonstration sources now support an Ultra Mobile PayGo Telegram registration-verification aggregate. Three report successful registration and two are mixed; number provenance and subsequent Telegram account state remain variable, so this is bounded evidence rather than a universal carrier probability.

H2O PayGo overseas continuity remains conflicted. A 2024 community recommendation reports PayGo Wi-Fi Calling and activation outside the United States, while the current PrepaidCompare profile says Wi-Fi Calling is monthly-plan only and a 2026 China-use guide reports recurring support resets may be needed. Current H2O terms still frame service as personal use in the U.S. only. Preserve HOLD and do not claim stable overseas SMS/OTP continuity.

Current first-party help confirms PAYG-only remains available, web/manual credit starts at $20, SMS top-ups can add $10 with a saved card, standalone PAYG expires 90 days after purchase, and first activation must occur on a U.S. network tower. International roaming also requires prior U.S. line use.

2026 community evidence is mixed for overseas SMS continuity: one Tello tutorial thread reports Codex verification SMS not arriving, while a separate long-running overseas user reports SMS/2FA abruptly stopping after months of Wi-Fi Calling. These reports do not isolate PAYG-only plan state tightly enough for a service aggregate, so preserve them as route-level risk evidence rather than manufacturing an app success rate.

Tello publicly acknowledges automated and human fraud-prevention checks can decline orders; community replies in the same provider-moderated thread describe account suspensions and concern about preserving long-held numbers. This is a continuity risk signal, not a quantified suspension probability.

The official RedPocket eBay store currently lists a distinct $30/360-day Starter Plan with unlimited talk/text and 200MB every 30 days, plus physical SIM, eSIM and renewal/existing-SIM options. This is not the website Essentials annual product and is normalized as a separate atomic route.

RedPocket requires activation in the United States. Wi-Fi Calling supports calls and SMS once provisioned, but a 2026 $30-plan user attempting setup abroad reported that support could enable the account flag yet full Wi-Fi Calling activation still could not be completed until returning to the U.S. Do not present this as a China-first activation route.

Current RedPocket help explicitly says eBay plans, including GSMA eBay plans, do not include international roaming. 2026 users nevertheless reported temporary roaming buckets on some $30-plan accounts and changing allowances. Treat those buckets as unstable/unpromised and rely on the provider exclusion for decision guidance.

The website Essentials annual route is kept separate from the distinct $30/360-day eBay Starter Plan. Current official Essentials annual page shows a $120 label, $80 first-year promotion, 3GB/month and $110 renewal; stale $60/$30 guide wording is removed from this canonical route.

Current KPN first-party pages price the prepaid SIM at €4.99. KPN Basis 2021 lists €0.15 per SMS. Credit has unlimited validity only if the line performs a qualifying action at least once every 6 months; incoming calls/SMS do not count. After 6 months of inactivity credit is frozen for 90 days, and a top-up during that rescue window can restore it; otherwise the number and credit are lost.
KPN moderator guidance in 2026 confirms KPN Prepaid does not support eSIM. Prepaid requires a physical SIM; subscription eSIM behavior must not be carried into this route.
Current provider-moderated guidance says a new KPN Prepaid SIM can only be activated in the Netherlands while connected to the KPN network. Abroad-first activation is not supported.

KPN officially supports prepaid abroad and states incoming SMS abroad is free, including outside the EU at destination-specific outgoing rates. A 2026 provider-community case reports a previously used prepaid line losing network abroad. Preserve this as an unquantified continuity risk rather than treating roaming/SMS reachability as guaranteed.

Current Three first-party pages no longer allow a new PAYG voice SIM to be ordered free on its own: a new SIM must be paired with a Data Pack, with the lowest currently displayed one-month Data Pack at £10. Standard PAYG rates remain 35p/min, 15p/text and 10p/MB. The number remains active only with at least one qualifying chargeable activity every 180 days; Wi-Fi-only activity does not count, and a disconnected number cannot be restored.
Three currently supports PAYG eSIM as well as physical SIM. Existing PAYG customers can request a replacement eSIM through My3 or the Three app, and new PAYG Data Pack offers can be selected as eSIM.

Before PAYG can be used abroad, Three requires the SIM/device to connect to the Three network in the UK and, if no allowance is preloaded, to top up or add a Data Pack in the UK. Three states receiving texts while roaming is free across the published PAYG destination bands, but destination/network availability is not treated as guaranteed.

Current Super first-party guidance still sells starter kits from €1 and confirms that calling-card service validity runs 180 days from activation or the last single top-up of at least €3. Splitting €3 into smaller top-ups does not extend validity. After expiry there is a 30-day receive/read/top-up rescue window; without a qualifying top-up the number and unused prepaid funds are lost.

Super continues to support both physical SIM and eSIM starter kits. Both standard SIM and eSIM can only be activated in Estonia; after activation the line can travel abroad with roaming enabled. Existing physical Super SIM cannot currently be converted directly to eSIM.

Roaming must be enabled before travel. In the EU, Super uses the same basic service price list as Estonia subject to fair-use rules. Outside the EU, operator prices vary and Super directs users to Telia roaming prices; this pass does not generalize non-EU inbound-SMS price or reachability into a reliability claim.

Super announced the basic standard-rate call and SMS price changing to €0.05 effective 24 September 2025. This does not replace the number-retention rule, which remains a single top-up of at least €3 every 180 days.

ALDI TALK currently advertises the Starter-Set at €2.99 through 2026-10-11, versus the regular €9.99 price, with €10 starting credit. Preserve €9.99 as the durable normalized acquisition baseline and record €2.99 only as a time-bounded promotion so a six-day sale does not become permanent route economics.

Current ALDI TALK guidance confirms a 12-month activity window after activation and a new activity window after each top-up. €5 gives 4 months and €30 gives 24 months; the existing official activity-window PDF supplies the full €5/€10/€15/€30 ladder. After the active window ends, the line remains reachable for two months but cannot actively call or use mobile data; without a top-up during that rescue period the SIM is deactivated.

The current dedicated ALDI TALK eSIM page offers a prepaid eSIM directly for online ordering and activation after registration, while the current SIM-service page still says eSIM is available only as an exchange card for an already activated plastic SIM. Preserve physical + eSIM capability but record the provider-documentation conflict instead of claiming one acquisition path is universally available.

ALDI TALK registration requires personal data and a valid accepted identity document. Online Video-Ident is available with camera, microphone and internet, and in-person identification options also exist. Reviewed first-party material does not establish universal China-first activation or universal acceptance of every foreign passport, so those outcomes remain unverified.

ALDI TALK officially supports prepaid roaming but warns that technical service restrictions can occur in some countries. The reviewed current first-party pages do not establish China-specific incoming-SMS reachability or app/OTP reliability, so no service-specific success claim or percentage is created.

Current 26 August 2026 Pantas terms say the plan is available to customers changing from another prepaid plan and charge RM2 for the successful rate-plan change. Current Hotlink Prepaid starter pricing is RM10. The Pantas FAQ still exposes legacy/direct starter-pack wording, so normalize a conservative current acquisition path as RM10 Hotlink Prepaid starter plus RM2 plan change rather than assuming a directly sold Pantas starter is universally available.

For eligible non-tourist Pantas service, Hotlink documents an RM30 365-day Active Period pass. After an ordinary active period ends, a 30-day Credit Grace Period allows incoming calls and SMS only; failing to top up before the grace period ends terminates the plan. The RM2/RM4/RM10 products with 365-day validity are internet passes, not SIM-validity substitutes.

Current Hotlink Pantas terms explicitly exclude tourist registrations from the normal Active Period, Credit Grace Period and 365-day SIM-validity clauses. Tourist service validity remains fixed at 90 days from original activation and is not extended, renewed or reset by plan switching, top-up or internet-pass purchase.

Hotlink supports new prepaid eSIM registration in the app and passport-based self-registration for non-Malaysians with ID scan and Face ID. These capabilities do not establish whether every non-Malaysian/passport registration is treated as a tourist under the 90-day lifecycle rule, so passport eligibility must not be equated with 365-day retention eligibility.

Hotlink Prepaid roaming is provisioned by default and relies on destination partner networks. A September 2026 Pantas user reported being unable to receive roaming SMS while the line and roaming were active; the user said support cited a minimum-balance requirement that was not published on the website. Other 2026 independent reports describe successful offshore eSIM setup only after adding sufficient prepaid balance. Preserve overseas incoming-SMS reachability as unquantified and balance-sensitive rather than guaranteed.

September 2026 users report the RM30/365-day validity option remains visible after switching to Pantas, including a reported RM2 plan-switch fee. This independently corroborates continued real-world availability but is not used to override first-party lifecycle or tourist rules.

FarEasTone's current regular prepaid page still offers NT$300 and NT$500 starter products. The number is valid for 180 days from activation and each qualifying recharge; current communication-credit recharge denominations include NT$100, NT$300, NT$500 and NT$1000. The lowest documented retention path therefore remains one NT$100 recharge per 180 days, approximately NT$200 per year.

FarEasTone maintains tourist prepaid products separately from the regular long-term 易付卡 line. The tourist-card page explicitly describes a short-term Taiwan-use product. Tourist inventory must not be used to infer long-term regular-prepaid lifecycle, roaming or retention economics.

FarEasTone currently advertises free incoming SMS abroad via international VoLTE for FarEasTone users when the handset and destination partner network support the service, and it maintains a prepaid-roaming portal. However, the reviewed sources do not explicitly bind the broad VoLTE/OTP claim to this exact regular-prepaid route in mainland China. Preserve overseas original-number SMS as plausible provider-supported capability but not a route-specific China guarantee.

A July 2026 long-term FarEasTone pay-as-you-go user reports repeated mismatches between FarEasTone and immigration records, requiring passport plus ARC updates and causing outgoing calling to be disabled when the update is not completed. Preserve this as an unquantified foreign-user identity-continuity risk rather than a universal failure claim.

FarEasTone's current regular-prepaid application remains an in-person Taiwan-store flow with two identity documents and customer-data registration. FarEasTone's current eSIM guide explicitly says prepaid-card users can use eSIM and that first application/change to eSIM is handled at a physical store with two identity documents. This supports physical + eSIM for the regular route, but does not establish offshore first activation.

Current TIM support states that a TIM Card is valid for 12 months from activation, the last recharge or another qualifying customer-requested commercial event. If none occurs, month 13 is receive-calls-and-SMS only, then the SIM/number is deactivated. TIM currently allows free number reactivation within a maximum 11 months after expiry.

TIM still sells Ricarica 5+ for EUR5. It includes EUR4 prepaid credit plus a temporary bundle. Because TIM explicitly resets card validity from the last recharge, EUR5 remains the lowest currently documented paid recharge action found in the reviewed first-party material for resetting the lifecycle clock. This is an annual retention action, not a claim that EUR5 of ordinary credit is added.

Current TIM mobile pages list a EUR10 one-time SIM cost for new prepaid customers. Online, EUR5 is prepaid credit and EUR5 is SIM activation; in TIM stores, EUR0.01 is residual credit and EUR9.99 is SIM activation. Offer-specific monthly charges are separate from this normalized SIM acquisition baseline.

TIM currently supports physical SIM and eSIM for new prepaid mobile customers, with online identification via SPID or video selfie. The online flow requires an Italian Codice Fiscale and a valid identity document; TIM explicitly lists passport among accepted identity documents for the switch-to-TIM flow. Card payment for that online flow is documented for cards issued in Italy, while courier identification can use cash. These requirements do not establish a frictionless offshore/non-resident first-activation path.

TIM currently markets use of the customer's TIM mobile number abroad and offers international roaming products, including China as a travel destination. The reviewed consumer pages do not provide exact regular-prepaid original-number incoming-SMS or app/OTP delivery guarantees for mainland China, so roaming existence must not be promoted as China OTP reliability.

Taiwan Mobile current regular 4G/5G prepaid tariff material includes standard NT$300 prepaid number-card products. Cheaper child, OK, light-data and short-term tourist variants are separate named products and are not used as the normalized acquisition baseline for this general long-term route.

Current Taiwan Mobile prepaid communication-credit recharge material includes an NT$100 recharge denomination and states that number validity restarts for six months from the recharge date. This establishes a lowest documented retention action of NT$100 every 180 days, about NT$200/year.

Taiwan Mobile currently supports eSIM for Taiwan Mobile prepaid users through physical stores; prepaid eSIM change/setup fees are deducted from prepaid balance. The page excludes legacy original Taiwan Star prepaid users, which does not change the Taiwan Mobile prepaid route identity.

Foreign applicants must use a physical myfone store and provide two original identity documents. Taiwan Mobile states that prepaid applicants are assigned either a short-validity card or a regular prepaid card according to the validity of their permitted stay in Taiwan. Online application is unavailable to international customers. Therefore passport acceptance alone does not guarantee eligibility for the long-term general-prepaid route.

Taiwan Mobile prepaid roaming explicitly states that in China the prepaid line does not provide roaming voice calling or outgoing SMS, but can receive SMS, excluding paid/premium SMS. Voice roaming must be enabled and device/network VoLTE conditions may apply. This is ordinary incoming-SMS entitlement, not an app/bank OTP delivery guarantee.

1pMobile current PAYG sales material shows a promotional signup price of £5 while supplying £10 of account credit, with £10 struck through as the ordinary price. A current joining FAQ still describes the normal join flow as paying £10 to add initial credit and receiving the SIM free. Preserve £10 as the durable normalized acquisition baseline and record the £5 offer as a current promotion rather than a permanent route-price rewrite.

For customers joining from 1 August 2026, 1pMobile requires at least £10 of spend/use every 90 days. If actual spend in a commitment period is below £10, the shortfall is deducted from account credit; if the balance is below £10, an automatic top-up is attempted from stored payment details. If the shortfall cannot be collected, service may be suspended immediately and the account may be closed after 10 days. This is a £10/90-day minimum consumption commitment, not a rule that a manual £10 top-up must occur every 90 days.

1pMobile supports eSIM for new customers at no eSIM charge, ordered online and activated from a QR code. Current help material states that a 1pMobile eSIM can often be activated while already outside the UK, but successful activation depends on the local roaming partner and is not guaranteed in every territory.

1pMobile current help material explicitly permits long-term use outside the UK in non-EU countries without a periodic UK-return requirement. It states that standard SMS, security verification codes, 2FA texts and banking OTP messages can continue to be received while roaming, subject to local network and roaming arrangements. Preserve this as provider-supported continuity, not a destination/app-specific measured success rate.

1pMobile currently documents Visa, MasterCard and PayPal as accepted payment methods and excludes American Express. The reviewed page does not establish universal acceptance of every non-UK-issued card, so foreign-card acceptance is not generalized beyond the named methods.

Mobal current roaming help separately states that international roaming is limited to the latest Voice+Data 5G SIM/eSIM products. Mobal Voice Lite eSIM is not delivered by email. Because voice products require identity verification under Mobal current Japanese-law process, the customer receives a physical eSIM access code by shipping to the verified ID address or collects it in Japan after showing a physical passport and order confirmation. Worldwide delivery is available where the destination-specific ID requirements can be met.
Mobal current Voice Lite documentation explicitly says Wi-Fi Calling is not supported. This route cannot use Wi-Fi Calling as a workaround for its Japan-only service boundary.

LABAS currently advertises direct eSIM entry from €1. The reviewed package page includes a €1 eSIM offer and a €1/month eSIM package with 1 GB, 100 minutes and 100 SMS. The €3 figure in the older profile is a qualifying retention top-up, not the current minimum direct acquisition price.

Current LABAS terms reconfirm that the account stays fully valid for 90 days from activation or the last top-up of at least €3. After 90 days without a qualifying top-up the line becomes receive-only for calls/SMS plus emergency outgoing; after 120 days the number is cancelled and cannot be restored.

LABAS currently requires prepaid registration and says citizens of any country can register online through biometric verification. Accepted online identity documents include passport, identity card, driver's licence or Lithuanian residence permit.

Remote identity registration does not establish universal offshore first activation. Current LABAS terms explicitly warn that service activation in foreign countries may be restricted under Lithuanian law, so the route must not be presented as guaranteed China-first or foreign-first activation.

LABAS current roaming material states that roaming allows customers to send and receive SMS abroad and lists China among supported non-EU roaming destinations. This supports ordinary roaming-SMS capability when registered on a partner network, but it is not evidence of bank/app OTP success.

Fortress currently lists the reusable physical haha SIM at HK$50 with HK$50 stored balance. The reviewed product page shows current direct Fortress availability with store pickup; the retained August 2026 independent thread also reports HK$50 Fortress online/store acquisition.

Current Fortress FAQ states that the SIM is valid for 365 days after activation and that each top-up of HK$10 or more extends validity by another 365 days. Purchasing a data package does not extend validity. An expired SIM may be considered for reactivation within 14 days, without guarantee; after more than 14 days it cannot be reactivated.
Fortress currently says haha SIM does not support eSIM and an existing physical haha SIM cannot be transferred to eSIM. The route remains physical-SIM-only.

Fortress requires real-name registration for Hong Kong local service and accepts HKID or applicable travel-document details for individual registration. The linked 3HK prepaid registration flow relies on the SIM obtaining network service and an SMS/OTP step. Reviewed official material does not establish a guaranteed mainland-China-first activation path.

Current Fortress FAQ supports roaming voice and SMS charged from stored balance and warns that related services cannot be used when balance is insufficient. This establishes ordinary roaming-SMS capability subject to service/balance conditions, not bank/app OTP reliability.

Current Fortress FAQ warns that random real-name-registration verification can suspend call/SMS service if required verification is not completed, and that recycled Hong Kong numbers can retain third-party platform history that may block social-app registration. These are material continuity risks independent of the low annual keep cost.

Current CelcomDigi prepaid acquisition surfaces support both physical SIM and Kuning eSIM entry, while the Kuning FAQ identifies a one-time RM5 SIM activation charge. No current first-party source reviewed here establishes RM10 as the complete lowest starter cost, so the prior RM10 acquisition metric is retired rather than treating the RM5 activation charge as a full SIM price.

For new prepaid activations from 26 August 2026, CelcomDigi requires Non-MyKad customers to register at an authorized dealer with original identification; foreign citizens must also provide valid student-visa or work-permit information. Malaysia's mandatory prepaid-registration standard separately limits tourist SIMs to a maximum of three months before automatic termination. CelcomDigi's current prepaid page advertises new Kuning eSIM packs, while the generic eSIM help page lists prepaid under conversion/replacement and restricts online-store eSIM sign-up to Malaysian citizens. Combined with the new Non-MyKad dealer-registration rule, eSIM remains technically supported but a fully remote foreign prepaid eSIM signup is not established.

Current CelcomDigi prepaid roaming material explicitly says customers can keep using their existing prepaid number for WhatsApp and OTPs overseas and lists China among the Asia roaming destinations. This is provider evidence for roaming-number continuity, not independent proof of any specific bank/app OTP path in mainland China.

A long-term Digi Prepaid user reported receiving SMS, including banking OTP use cases, while roaming in Singapore without buying a roaming plan, provided the SIM attached to the local network and mobile data roaming remained off. This is one historical independent operational report and is not generalized to all destinations or services.

Current e& prepaid shopping surfaces advertise a AED40 Wasel prepaid SIM/eSIM entry with AED40 pre-loaded credit. This is treated as the current online acquisition offer, not as a permanent historical connection-fee baseline.

Current Wasel terms define 90 consecutive days of inactivity across recharge, calls and non-promotional SMS as the lifecycle trigger. Qualifying use can include making or receiving calls and sending or receiving SMS. If inactivity continues and balance is sufficient, e& debits AED10 for each 90-day period; if the service is suspended, the mobile number is retained for one year before permanent disconnection.

The lowest current provider-published controllable UAE keep action is a local SMS at AED0.19. Sending one before each 90-day inactivity deadline implies about AED0.76/year in local-use conditions. Standard rest-of-world roaming SMS is AED2, so an abroad-controlled SMS path is roughly AED8/year where a roaming partner is available. The AED10/90-day inactivity debit is a fallback, not the cheapest active-use path.

Regular Wasel purchase requires a valid Emirates ID for UAE nationals/residents. Visitors use the separate Visitor Line; migrating that visitor product to Wasel requires visiting an e& outlet with a new Emirates ID. Passport-only visitor eligibility is therefore not generalized into long-term Wasel eligibility.

Wasel's current product surface exposes eSIM, but e&'s current eSIM help says requesting or activating eSIM requires location access and physical presence in the UAE. Offshore first activation is not treated as supported.

Current Wasel support says incoming SMS while roaming is supported and free. Current standard roaming rates likewise list incoming SMS as free, and the roaming FAQ documents prepaid recharge while abroad through the e& UAE app or vouchers. This establishes provider capability, not universal bank/app OTP delivery reliability.

One independent Etisalat Wasel Prepaid user reported retaining overseas signal and successfully receiving UAEPass OTP while travelling. This is a single historical route-level success signal, not a success-rate sample.

An independent Wasel discussion describes free roaming SMS/verification reception abroad and maintaining the line with periodic activity. It is retained as historical community corroboration only; exact destination, bank and app reliability are not inferred.

The August 2026 NCC Quality of Service Business Rules say a prepaid line may be deactivated after six months without a Revenue Generating Event and may lose the number after another six months. The same rules count parked numbers as an RGE, exclude bare recharge without follow-up qualifying activity, and require alternative-means notice at least 14 days before churn. MTN's current prepaid terms separately state a 365-day no-RGE disconnection rule, so the conflict is preserved instead of collapsed into one inactivity clock.
MTN currently supports eSIM, but first eSIM setup requires visiting an MTN store for device eligibility checks and a QR code. This does not establish remote China-first activation.

A 2026 independent Nairaland report says an MTN Nigeria number was reassigned despite the user reporting an active Keep My Number subscription and ongoing recharge. Treat this as a single-user continuity incident, not proof that KMN generally fails.
RUB349/6 months, initial immediate debit and renewal from sufficient balance on eligible tariffs; this is not an acquisition price.

Ordinary no-monthly-fee inactivity is distinct from subscribed number-retention. MTS says 30 inactive days may trigger RUB1.5/day until available balance runs out, then possible contract termination after six months.
Foreign citizens need passport/Gosuslugi/biometrics in Russia. A new eSIM first activates only on Russia's own MTS network; offshore/China-first activation is not demonstrated.
MTS documents a conditional 24-hour SMS/data restriction after returning from abroad or >72 hours offline, with early lifting after device verification. It is not a universal overseas OTP rate.
An independent MTS user reported incoming roaming-SMS failure until roaming was enabled; this report is general MTS roaming and not tested on this retention add-on or a specific app.
Archived Номер навсегда RUB1,500 one-time may be a distinct historical product. Availability and scope are unverified; do not conflate with current Сохраняю номер RUB349/6 months.

GO na den CZK29 daily rate starts on first outbound call or mobile data connection. SMS is charged separately; incoming SMS alone is not listed as a trigger. Unintended mobile data can create extra spend.

O2 online CZK300–9,999 card top-up requires internet-payments-enabled card issued in Europe. Retail cash/card top-up is offered. Non-European payment acceptance is not established.

One independent r/Prague user described buying an O2 physical prepaid SIM in a Prague retail service point. This supports local acquisition only; the reported bundle is not proven to be the present GO na den CZK99 SKU, and no China/OTP claim is inferred.
The exact lowest official 12-month Telstra Pre-Paid Casual recharge is AUD74; the separate data-rich Pre-Paid Mobile 12-month offer is AUD395 and does not define the lowest number-retention cost.

Telstra documents 6 months of recharge-only recovery following recharge expiry, then prepaid line deactivation and number loss. Receiving calls is supported in that window, but the support text does not affirm inbound SMS.

Current checkout offers prepaid Casual eSIM or a AUD2 physical SIM starter plus recharge; an international passport appears on the accepted-ID selection but successful offshore-first eSIM activation is not confirmed.

Current Telstra roaming copy describes pack allowances; independent 2026 prepaid reports disagree over needing a roaming pack for incoming SMS. No China/OTP app-level conclusion or exact service observation follows.
One independent long-validity Telstra prepaid user reported being unable to purchase an international roaming pack while already overseas; retain as one incident, not a universal failure rate.

The old BRL15/90 days and BRL60/year normalization is not the currently listed recharge product. Current provider table specifies BRL35/90 days; four recharges are BRL140 for 360 days, with no verified total acquisition cost.

Claro cancellation FAQ uses both '90 days after the last recharge' and '90 days of validity of the last recharge' language; a later 180-day reassignment risk is a separate after-deactivation event, NOT a guaranteed credit-validity or usable-service period.

Claro explicitly states prepaid and Controle subscribers do not have international roaming and must change to a postpaid product. Free inbound international SMS stated on postpaid roaming terms does not apply to this prepaid route.

Claro's current eSIM FAQ supports a foreign passport for prepaid eSIM but only at physical stores; online access is not proof of foreign offshore-first onboarding. Independent January 2026 tourist reports a Claro shop refusing passport activation.

One user complained on 2026-02-19 of buying Claro prepaid eSIM but being unable to first-activate from Portugal, with support indicating physical Brazil presence was needed. One report, not a universal probability.

A June 2026 self-identified Claro prepaid user outside Brazil reported no international roaming and inability to switch their line to postpaid remotely. Independently corroborates provider restriction without an app-specific success percentage.

The provider says a chargeable call or SMS every 180 days keeps the number active, while a separate top-up/plan-credit rule demands a recharge or bundle within 180 days to avoid restricted outgoing service. Both clocks need attention; a lone SMS cannot be guaranteed to reset top-up credit.

After 180 days without top-up/plan purchase the account restricts outbound service but explicitly allows inbound calls/texts; after a further 90 days without contacting support and paying, the number and balance can be irretrievably lost.

Official PAYG terms give £5 minimum top-up. Current online card payment explicitly accepts Visa/Mastercard only with UK-registered billing address; foreign-issued cards/addresses cannot be assumed accepted.

Provider Sept 2025 PAYG rate book lists China in World Group 1 and outgoing SMS to UK at £0.20, but does not quantify receiving SMS abroad or prove any Chinese bank/OTP reception. A UK-only credit/card requirement raises continuity risk.

Official physical PAYG SIM activates on supported UK network when first used and online account links via inbound verification SMS; provider offers physical-to-eSIM conversion but no proven foreign first activation flow or same onboarding for a new PAYG eSIM.

One March 2026 ASDA subscriber describes setting a reminder to send a text around 5.5 months. This is a single lived usage report, not evidence that text-only waives the different official 180-day top-up-credit expiry rule.
One June 2022 PAYG customer reports no received 180-day warning or disconnection shortly after the 180-day mark. Historical anecdote, not a guaranteed cancellation window.

SMS sent while overseas continue over cellular despite VoWiFi support.
2023 first-hand Free €2 SMS 2FA receipt in unspecified Asian country; app/bank and China not identified.

January 2026 Canadian users reported Christmas-period service/account access failures after migration, and support calls ending without resolution. This is a bounded user report, not a universal outage rate.

March 2026 migrated users reported legacy CAD350-500 balances suddenly displayed as zero after CAD19 monthly renewals, customer service unreachable and one reported number going out of service; unverified individually and not universal.

O2 online credit-card top-ups require a UK-bank card with UK-registered billing address, from £10 in pounds; vouchers/cash machine alternatives are not evidence of foreign signup funding.
O2 offers eSIM for eligible current PAYG and existing SIM swaps, but this is not evidence that a legacy Classic line is entitled to a Classic-specific eSIM exchange or offshore first activation.
General O2 PAYG Wi-Fi Calling exists but is currently unsupported outside the UK; do not present international Wi-Fi Calling as an OTP workaround.
Official O2 roaming pages do not verify Classic-specific China incoming SMS entitlement or exact bank/app OTP success; avoid blanket claims of free global incoming SMS.
One 2024 Classic customer reported disconnection despite claimed chargeable calls inside six months and required four support contacts to regain account access; anecdotal, not a line-loss percentage.
A self-described 2025 Classic holder reports continued 3p calling/2p SMS use and worries about 3G/2G device connectivity; the report establishes legacy active users, not new-sale availability.

A November-December 2025 O2 forum thread contains two existing Classic lines still shown as Classic and other users reporting account relabeling, auto-top-up loss and calls abroad failing; mixed tariffs, not proof Classic-wide roaming failure.
Singtel-authorised Tourist tariff shows S$15/30-day and S$30/30-day variants; S$10/7-day is separate. The former S$12 offer is not the currently verified public 30-day baseline.

Singtel tourist page explicitly limits passport-registered SIMs of all forms to data-only, and tourist eSIM likewise data-only. Headline bundled calls/SMS in a plan table do not override registration-specific policy.

China is a data-roaming destination in S$15 and higher tourist plans. Terms expressly separate data bundles from SMS/voice availability; no China inbound bank/app OTP promise.

For generic Singtel prepaid (NOT tourist passport SIM), help says incoming overseas SMS still depends on 3G availability, and outgoing roaming SMS is unsupported. Do not transfer to passport tourist data-only service.
Nov 2024 tourist eSIM user reports visible +65 number but no calls/SMS or hi!App OTP; 2025 follow-up likewise reports lack of voice/text, corroborating restriction, not all future variants.

Jan 2026 follow-up on a Dec 2025 tourist eSIM reports hi!App unusable because login demands SMS OTP unavailable on data-only eSIM. Specific hi!App failure, not an invented bank OTP success percentage.

July 2026 Reddit author quotes Singtel support email suggesting eKYC passport-only data activation in Malaysia before entering Singapore; seller attribution remains unverified and does not prove China-first voice/SMS.
January 2025 tourist eSIM buyer reports passport recognition/eKYC failure and difficult support; reply recommends in-person Singtel store. One incident, no aggregate rejection rate.

April 2025 non-tourist Singtel prepaid holder says support confirmed UK incoming SMS requires 3G; second-user Australia claim. Adjacent regular-prepaid continuity concern; does not establish China tourist-SIM OTP.

Official True Jaidee confirms *934*30/90/180# validity-extension USSD format effective July 1, 2026, replacing prior IVR. Official accessible page does not independently show the price or eligibility ladder.

Independent Jan-2026 Thai guide reports THB3/30d, THB9/90d and THB15/180d, conditional on at least 90 days SIM age or cumulative THB200 usage; price is not provider-checkout verified. Two 180-day buys imply THB30/360d only if eligibility and repeat purchases hold.

Since May 14, 2026, standard prepaid with expired active validity and remaining balance may enter automatic THB3 per 30-day number-retention billing for at most 180 days. This is a limited post-expiry rescue, not an active-usage/roaming-OTP guarantee; further suspension is possible.

First-party Thailand Tourist SIM terms cap tourist-SIM validity at 60 days; after expiry, top-ups cannot extend it and passport re-identification is required. Short-term Tourist SIMs are expressly excluded from the automatic number-retention program.

True international roaming FAQ says prepaid customers may enable overseas voice/SMS-related roaming by dialing *118*001# free while still in Thailand. This is not proof of mainland China OTP connectivity or of first activation abroad.

First-party True App prepaid registration supports identity-document/passport entry and face eKYC; eligibility for a non-tourist long-lived number under foreign passport is not established by generic registration guidance.

March 2026 user reported prepaid line valid and topped up yet no foreign network; same thread later reports support-enabled incoming SMS after roaming-package purchase, while another commenter still failed after package purchase. This is mixed anecdotal evidence, not a failure rate or China sample.

Firsthand U.S.-based user of a TrueMove Thai number could not receive OTP to top up while abroad; a different commenter says a paid preserve-number service enabled U.S. banking OTP. Plan details differ and this does not establish a success percentage.

BTK Decision 2026/IK-THD/125 struck out the former passport→YKN 90-day conversion procedure, 91st-day outbound restriction and 181st-day shutdown with effect 2026-06-25. The current 90-day tourist advance-application allowance is a different clock; neither proves open-ended service.

Turkcell Tourist official flow: order no more than 90 days before intended Türkiye arrival; valid passport for Tourist line; app eSIM activation needs chipped passport, NFC/eSIM phone, liveness/video contract; service becomes usable upon Türkiye entry. Package allowance applies only within Türkiye.

Current ordinary Turkcell prepaid FAQ specifies one TRY200 or higher top-up/transfer yields 185 active days plus up to 180 semi-active days. Earlier mirrored provider pages still show TRY10 minimum, creating first-party page divergence; none establishes that the ordinary 185/180-day rule or minimum applies to foreign Tourist SIM.

Turkcell's standard mobile prepaid support lists the 2026 annual radio-use levy as TRY323.81, collected in installments subject to any arrears. This is generic tax context, not evidence that Tourist SIM incurs a specific yearly renewal fee or that paying it preserves its number.

May 2026 thread: tourist reported repeated local prepaid SIM sales refusals by several shops; a separate visitor reports obtaining and activating a Turkcell tourist SIM at a store for around EUR25. Mixed seller reports, not a measured eligibility denial rate.

September 2026 visitor reports paying TRY1,800 for a Turkcell Tourist SIM in a store. One independent localized purchase anecdote; actual currently selectable official Tourist package/checkout total and tax composition remain unknown.

Former Türkiye resident with Turkcell banking-number reported loss of reception in Lebanon despite enabled roaming; later said Wi-Fi Calling restored access. Tourist plan identity unspecified, geography Lebanon not China, and app bank OTP delivery itself not quantified.

A former Türkiye resident abroad with a PAYG Turkcell line reports no service and inability to receive SMS needed for Turkcell login; replies discuss unpaid radio tax, recharge and roaming as possibilities, not confirmed cause or tourist-specific failure.

2026 foreign-device Turkcell customer reported locally blocked phone/IMEI while their SIM functioned in another phone. Distinguish device registration/IMEI restriction from SIM-number expiry or passport service shutdown; individual incident, not proof of Tourist rule.
